A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same end-to-end LLM watermarking work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark detection, text-quality, translation, code-generation, ablation and efficiency results, including repeated-trial significance tests in Appendix I.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original watermark-theft experiments, decoder comparisons, corpus statistics and training-stability analyses.

M1.justification: The core encoder-decoder architecture, losses, online prompting and cross-LLM converter remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a limited extension using a key-driven binary logit bias on top-k candidates and fine-tuning to obtain distinct watermarks.

E1.justification: v3 adds watermark-theft evaluation on Dolly CW and MMW BookReports, extending evaluation beyond ordinary text modifications. Table 14 also adds green-list-ratio measurements on five corpora: xsum, StackOverflow-QA-C-Language-40k, ML-ArXiv-Papers, mimic-cxr-dataset and finance-alpaca. The original training and downstream-task datasets are retained.

E2.justification: The existing accuracy-comparison baseline sets are retained. The efficiency study expands from measurements of the proposed method alone to a direct comparison with KGW, Unbiased and EXP-Edit in v3 Table 19; EXP-Edit was previously discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include 2,000-query spoofing attacks, TPR at a fixed 1% FPR, context-size comparisons and evaluation of a variant fine-tuned for 5,000 steps. The stated training batch size also changes from 16 in v1 Table 8 to 8 in v3 Table 15. This reporting change does not establish that the retained benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices B.2-B.5 and C.2 substantially expand analysis through edited-text neural-versus-statistical decoder comparisons, context-size ablations, watermark-theft and mitigation tests, green-list statistics, token-distribution bias and training stability. Existing length, temperature, sampling and component ablations remain.

E5.justification: v3 adds three from-scratch training runs of 5,000 steps with seeds 63, 64 and 65, plus mean and standard deviation reporting for corpus-level green-list ratios. The five generation trials, shared-seed practice, paired t-tests and uncertainty values from v1 Appendix I are retained in v3 Appendix A.6.

E6.justification: The original benchmark tables retain their numerical results, while v3 adds substantial security, decoder, bias, stability and timing results. Its new fine-tuning comparison reports PPL of 7.28 versus 7.73, but paraphrasing TPR of 0.53 versus 0.75 at 1% FPR (Table 13). These compare variants within v3, not improved performance of the unchanged method across versions. Some summary percentages also change, including 17.2% to 17.3% in Section 4.2.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a conditional mathematical argument for distinct keyed watermarks: independent uniform binary assumptions produce a Bin(k, 0.5) mismatch model and an identical-watermark probability of 2^-20 for k=20. The original method equations and tokenizer-alignment calculation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: joint encoder-decoder optimization, differentiable online prompting, a robustness-quality advantage and cross-LLM transfer without additional training. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands explanations of robustness through neural decoding and adaptive context dependence, and explains temperature effects through top-logit selection. It newly discusses watermark-theft vulnerability, mitigation costs and the tradeoff between token-distribution bias and robustness. These materially qualify the method's practical behavior beyond v1's discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link and documents a consequential three-stage curriculum: detection alone before 10k steps, joint objectives during 10k-20k, and online paraphrasing after 20k. It also revises the batch-size disclosure and specifies keyed fine-tuning details. The curriculum is newly documented; the PDFs do not establish that it replaced a different earlier schedule.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bengio et al. on curriculum learning and Jovanovic et al. on watermark stealing to support the new training discussion and security evaluation. The main related-work section and positioning against existing watermarking approaches remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendix is substantially reorganized from separate A-K sections into thematic A-E groups with nested subsections and a contents page. Existing significance tests, training details and editing examples are regrouped. Main-text copyediting, revised cross-references, acknowledgements and an impact statement accompany this structural revision.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven tables and two figures presenting the new analyses. Figures 1-10 are retained with layout adjustments, while existing tables receive clearer metric and task labels. Figure 8's incorrect ROC-curve caption is corrected to describe sentence-length detection performance.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves scrutiny of the robustness claims through fixed-FPR decoder comparisons, mechanism analyses and explicit watermark-theft testing that v1 lacked. The security extension's reduced paraphrasing TPR is reported, making its practical tradeoff visible. Documenting the training curriculum and code access also improves reproducibility information. These gains materially strengthen the paper despite unchanged main benchmark results and the limited 5,000-step scope of the new training-stability study.
